title: Sehwag's 70 Not Out Powers India U-19 To 10-Wicket Win Over Nepal
excerpt: Aaryavir Sehwag made 70 not out and captain Lakshya Raichandani 53 not out as India chased 129 in 19.1 overs, after bowling Nepal out for 128 in their U-19 Asia Cup opener in Al Amerat.
body:
• India Under-19 beat Nepal Under-19 by 10 wickets in their opening Group A match of the ACC Men's U-19 Asia Cup at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground on Friday, November 6.
  • Nepal were bowled out for 128 in 42.3 overs, with Ishan Sood taking 3 for 18 and Arjun Rajput 3 for 8.
  • Aaryavir Sehwag, son of former India opener Virender Sehwag, finished 70 not out and captain Lakshya Raichandani 53 not out as India reached 129 for no loss in 19.1 overs, with 185 balls to spare.
  • The win took India to the top of Group A with two points and a net run rate of 4.170, and they next face Pakistan in their second Group A match on Sunday.

India opened their ACC Men's Under-19 Asia Cup campaign with a 10-wicket win over Nepal at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground on Friday. Chasing 129, India reached 129 for no loss in 19.1 overs, completing the result with 185 balls remaining after Nepal had been bowled out for 128 in 42.3 overs, Bilkul Online reported.

Bowlers set up the win

India elected to bowl first, and Ishan Sood led the attack with 3 for 18 from his 10 overs, including four maidens. Arjun Rajput took 3 for 8, and Yashveer Goud took two wickets as Nepal's innings ended in the 43rd over, SportsTak reported.

Darsh Sonar held Nepal's innings together with 43 off 93 balls. He added 24 with Niraj Yadav and 43 with Aashish Luhar, who made 29, to take Nepal past 100 before the lower order fell away once that partnership was broken, Bilkul Online reported.

Openers finish the chase unbeaten

Aaryavir Sehwag and Lakshya Raichandani then made the chase a formality. Sehwag, the son of former India opener Virender Sehwag, attacked the Nepal spinners and reached his half-century off 34 balls. Raichandani, the captain, brought up his own fifty off 59 balls and finished 53 not out off 63 balls, with seven boundaries, according to SportsTak.

Sehwag finished 70 not out, and the pair's unbroken opening stand took India home in the 20th over. Because no wicket fell, no other India batter was required to bat.

What it means and what comes next

The margin mattered as well as the points. Bilkul Online reported that the win, completed with 185 balls remaining, put India at the top of Group A with two points and a net run rate of 4.170.

India's second Group A match is against Pakistan on Sunday. Nepal, after being bowled out for 128 and losing by 10 wickets, will need a result in their remaining group matches to recover from the opening defeat. For India, the immediate test is whether the same bowling control and opening partnership can be repeated against Pakistan, a stronger opponent than the side they dismissed on Friday.
